questions.q: Rationalise the denominator and simplify: $\frac{10}{3 - \sqrt{5}}$.
questions.target: Name, identify, order, and compare fractions
questions.answer: Multiply numerator and denominator by the conjugate $3 + \sqrt{5}$: $\frac{10(3 + \sqrt{5})}{(3 - \sqrt{5})(3 + \sqrt{5})} = \frac{10(3 + \sqrt{5})}{9 - 5} = \frac{10(3 + \sqrt{5})}{4} = \frac{5(3 + \sqrt{5})}{2} = \frac{15 + 5\sqrt{5}}{2}$. [M1 for multiplying by conjugate, M1 for difference of squares denominator, A1 for simplified form]
questions.explanation: Multiply numerator and denominator by the conjugate $3 + \sqrt{5}$: $\frac{10(3 + \sqrt{5})}{(3 - \sqrt{5})(3 + \sqrt{5})} = \frac{10(3 + \sqrt{5})}{9 - 5} = \frac{10(3 + \sqrt{5})}{4} = \frac{5(3 + \sqrt{5})}{2} = \frac{15 + 5\sqrt{5}}{2}$. [M1 for multiplying by conjugate, M1 for difference of squares denominator, A1 for simplified form]

questions.q: A bag contains 6 green counters and 4 yellow counters. A counter is chosen at random, its colour recorded, and it is REPLACED. A second counter is then chosen. What is the probability that both counters are the same colour?
questions.answer: Since the counter is replaced, events are independent: $P(\mathrm{Green,\ Green}) = \left(\frac{6}{10}\right)^2 = \frac{36}{100}$ $P(\mathrm{Yellow,\ Yellow}) = \left(\frac{4}{10}\right)^2 = \frac{16}{100}$ $P(\mathrm{Same\ Colour}) = \frac{36}{100} + \frac{16}{100} = \frac{52}{100} = \frac{13}{25}.$
questions.explanation: Since the counter is replaced, events are independent: $P(\mathrm{Green,\ Green}) = \left(\frac{6}{10}\right)^2 = \frac{36}{100}$ $P(\mathrm{Yellow,\ Yellow}) = \left(\frac{4}{10}\right)^2 = \frac{16}{100}$ $P(\mathrm{Same\ Colour}) = \frac{36}{100} + \frac{16}{100} = \frac{52}{100} = \frac{13}{25}.$

questions.q: A car travels a distance of 150 km, correct to the nearest 10 km, in a time of 2 hours, correct to the nearest 0.1 hour. What is the upper bound of the average speed in km/h?
questions.answer: Upper bound of speed = $\frac{\mathrm{Upper\ bound\ of\ distance}}{\mathrm{Lower\ bound\ of\ time}}$. Upper distance = $150 + 5 = 155$ km. Lower time = $2.0 - 0.05 = 1.95$ hours. Maximum speed = $\frac{155}{1.95} \approx 79.487$ km/h $\approx 79.5$ km/h. [M1 for upper dist / lower time, A1 for 79.5]
questions.explanation: Upper bound of speed = $\frac{\mathrm{Upper\ bound\ of\ distance}}{\mathrm{Lower\ bound\ of\ time}}$. Upper distance = $150 + 5 = 155$ km. Lower time = $2.0 - 0.05 = 1.95$ hours. Maximum speed = $\frac{155}{1.95} \approx 79.487$ km/h $\approx 79.5$ km/h. [M1 for upper dist / lower time, A1 for 79.5]

questions.q: In a survey of 50 tourists, 30 visited museum $M$, 25 visited palace $P$, and 20 visited art gallery $G$. 12 visited both $M$ and $P$, 10 visited both $P$ and $G$, 8 visited both $M$ and $G$, and 5 visited all three. How many tourists visited NONE of the three attractions?
questions.answer: By the 3-set inclusion-exclusion principle: $n(M \cup P \cup G) = (30 + 25 + 20) - (12 + 10 + 8) + 5 = 75 - 30 + 5 = 50$. Since the union equals 50, all 50 tourists visited at least one attraction. Therefore, $50 - 50 = 0$ tourists visited none. [M1 for 3-set formula, A1 for 50, A1 for 0]
questions.explanation: By the 3-set inclusion-exclusion principle: $n(M \cup P \cup G) = (30 + 25 + 20) - (12 + 10 + 8) + 5 = 75 - 30 + 5 = 50$. Since the union equals 50, all 50 tourists visited at least one attraction. Therefore, $50 - 50 = 0$ tourists visited none. [M1 for 3-set formula, A1 for 50, A1 for 0]

questions.q: A bank account pays compound interest of 3% per year. How many complete years will it take for an initial deposit of USD 2000 to exceed USD 3000?
questions.answer: We need $2000(1.03)^n > 3000 \Rightarrow (1.03)^n > 1.5$. Taking logarithms: $n \ln(1.03) > \ln(1.5) \Rightarrow n > \frac{\ln(1.5)}{\ln(1.03)} \approx \frac{0.405465}{0.029559} \approx 13.72$. The minimum number of complete years is 14. [M1 for setting up inequality, A1 for 14 years]
questions.explanation: We need $2000(1.03)^n > 3000 \Rightarrow (1.03)^n > 1.5$. Taking logarithms: $n \ln(1.03) > \ln(1.5) \Rightarrow n > \frac{\ln(1.5)}{\ln(1.03)} \approx \frac{0.405465}{0.029559} \approx 13.72$. The minimum number of complete years is 14. [M1 for setting up inequality, A1 for 14 years]

questions.q: Port $B$ is 40 km from Port $A$ on a bearing of $120^\circ$. Port $C$ is 50 km from Port $A$ on a bearing of $030^\circ$. Calculate the distance between Port $B$ and Port $C$.
questions.answer: The angle between the two paths at Port $A$ is $120^\circ - 030^\circ = 90^\circ$. Since this is a right triangle, use Pythagoras: $BC = \sqrt{40^2 + 50^2} = \sqrt{1600 + 2500} = \sqrt{4100} \approx 64.03$ km $\approx 64.0$ km. [M1 for angle at A = 90, M1 for Pythagoras, A1 for 64.0]
questions.explanation: The angle between the two paths at Port $A$ is $120^\circ - 030^\circ = 90^\circ$. Since this is a right triangle, use Pythagoras: $BC = \sqrt{40^2 + 50^2} = \sqrt{1600 + 2500} = \sqrt{4100} \approx 64.03$ km $\approx 64.0$ km. questions.q: A drawer contains 5 blue socks, 4 grey socks, and 3 black socks. Two socks are pulled at random without replacement. What is the probability of pulling two socks of different colours?
questions.target: Name, identify, order, and compare fractions
questions.answer: Total socks = 12. Total pairs = $\binom{12}{2} = 66$. Number of same-colour pairs: $\binom{5}{2} + \binom{4}{2} + \binom{3}{2} = 10 + 6 + 3 = 19.$ Therefore, the probability that the two socks have different colours is: $P(\mathrm{Different}) = 1 - \frac{19}{66} = \frac{47}{66}.$
questions.explanation: Total socks = 12. Total pairs = $\binom{12}{2} = 66$. Number of same-colour pairs: $\binom{5}{2} + \binom{4}{2} + \binom{3}{2} = 10 + 6 + 3 = 19.$ Therefore, the probability that the two socks have different colours is: $P(\mathrm{Different}) = 1 - \frac{19}{66} = \frac{47}{66}.$

questions.q: Convert $0.1\dot{4}\dot{8}$ to a fraction in its simplest form.
questions.answer: Let $x = 0.1484848\ldots$. Then $10x = 1.484848\ldots$ and $1000x = 148.484848\ldots$. Subtract: $1000x - 10x = 148 - 1 = 147 \Rightarrow 990x = 147 \Rightarrow x = \frac{147}{990}$. Divide numerator and denominator by 3: $\frac{49}{330}$. [M1 for 1000x - 10x, A1 for 49/330]
questions.explanation: Let $x = 0.1484848\ldots$. Then $10x = 1.484848\ldots$ and $1000x = 148.484848\ldots$. Subtract: $1000x - 10x = 148 - 1 = 147 \Rightarrow 990x = 147 \Rightarrow x = \frac{147}{990}$. Divide numerator and denominator by 3: $\frac{49}{330}$. [M1 for 1000x - 10x, A1 for 49/330]

questions.q: In a circle of radius 10 cm, an arc subtends a central angle of $72^\circ$. Calculate the perimeter of this sector to 1 decimal place.
questions.answer: Arc length: $s = \frac{72}{360} \times 2\pi(10) = \frac{1}{5} \times 20\pi = 4\pi \approx 12.57$ cm. Perimeter of sector = arc + 2 radii = $12.57 + 2(10) = 32.57 \approx 32.6$ cm. [M1 for arc length, M1 for adding 2r, A1 for 32.6]
questions.explanation: Arc length: $s = \frac{72}{360} \times 2\pi(10) = \frac{1}{5} \times 20\pi = 4\pi \approx 12.57$ cm. Perimeter of sector = arc + 2 radii = $12.57 + 2(10) = 32.57 \approx 32.6$ cm. [M1 for arc length, M1 for adding 2r, A1 for 32.6]

questions.q: A vertical pole of height 12 m casts a shadow of length 9 m on horizontal ground. Calculate the angle of elevation of the sun to the nearest degree.
questions.answer: Use tangent: $\tan\theta = \frac{\mathrm{opposite}}{\mathrm{adjacent}} = \frac{12}{9} \approx 1.333 \Rightarrow \theta = \tan^{-1}(1.333) \approx 53.1^\circ \approx 53^\circ$. [M1 for tan(theta)=12/9, A1 for 53]
questions.explanation: Use tangent: $\tan\theta = \frac{\mathrm{opposite}}{\mathrm{adjacent}} = \frac{12}{9} \approx 1.333 \Rightarrow \theta = \tan^{-1}(1.333) \approx 53.1^\circ \approx 53^\circ$. [M1 for tan(theta)=12/9, A1 for 53]
